notes.point: Respondent alleges eviction ground under S.14(1)(b) based on tenant sub-letting premises to United Automobiles without written consent, relying on an unregistered lease clause permitting such assignment to 'associate concerns'.

Appellant argues United Automobiles is an authorized distributor/agent, not a sub-tenant, and the unregistered lease clause granting permission to assign to associates is admissible for collateral purposes despite non-registration under S.49 of Registration Act 1908 (p0004.s001, p0004.s004).

RC-01 establishes that S.14(1)(b) applies if tenant sub-lets/assigns/parts with possession on/after 9.6.1952 without written landlord consent; voluntariness is irrelevant, but this rule requires verifying the specific 'written consent' exception in the lease and the legal status of the sub-lessee (p0004.s005, p0004.s006).

Critical gap: The record lacks the Rent Controller's specific finding on whether the lease clause's 'associate concern' exception was legally valid or if United Automobiles qualified as such, leaving the applicability of S.14(1)(b) factually unresolved (p0004.s002, p0004.s003).

RC-02 distinguishes corporate amalgamation from this case; here, the appellant is a single company (Bajaj Auto) and the sub-lessee is a separate entity (United Automobiles), so corporate succession defenses do not apply (p0003.s003, p0004.s003).

RC-05 is inapplicable as the record shows no late procedural plea; the dispute concerns the substantive interpretation of the lease terms and the definition of 'sub-letting' versus 'agency' under the Act (p0004.s001, p0004.s003).

proposal.coverage_limits: The supplied text contains party arguments and the lease clause but omits the lower courts' final factual findings on whether the 'associate concern' exception was satisfied or if the sub-lessee status was definitively established, which are necessary to apply RC-01.
